q1_issues.issue: (Inheritance wintergloss gloss) decomposes a closed single-word coinage, whereas the compound-kind genus is licensed for symbols fused from a multi-word surface form; nothing in the text says a wintergloss is a gloss.
(Inheritance nightmoth moth) is the same closed-single-word decomposition, emitted here although the compound section as written does not reach it.

q2_gaps: whether a closed single-word compound coinage ("wintergloss", "nightmoth") takes the compound-kind genus atom that the instruction set licenses only for surface-fused multi-word compounds

a demonstrative definite in a conditional's consequent that co-varies with the antecedent ("that lantern" = the lantern the wintergloss burns in): an antecedent-less definite is given a fresh constant, with no way to make it depend on the rule variable
notes: The conditional itself is well formed - variable trigger event, Skolem-function response over both universals, a During link, 1.0 / 0.9 - and Patient on the intransitive burn subject is right. A consequence of sk_lantern_1 being a rule-external constant is that every burning ends up sharing the same one lantern, but the instruction set offers no licensed alternative.
